ProteinBench

Can frontier reasoning models solve real structural biology problems from weights and reasoning alone, with no alignments, no structure predictors and no databases?

Talu Gueloglu

Paper Results Explorer All 522 datapoints Code

Abstract

A protein is a linear chain of amino acids that folds without help into one particular three-dimensional shape, and nearly everything it does — catalysing a reaction, recognising a partner, carrying a signal — follows from that shape. Three questions sit at the centre of the field: what structure does a given chain adopt, what chain would produce a structure you want, and how much does changing a single residue cost in stability or in binding. All three are physics problems about packing, hydrogen bonding and burial of hydrophobic surface, and none of them is answerable by reading the amino-acid letters one at a time.

Language models are trained on protein sequences together with the literature and databases that describe them, so a model can produce a correct-looking answer either by reasoning about that physics or by recalling a structure it has already read. ProteinBench is built to tell those apart. It is an eight-task suite of 522 targets covering forward folding, inverse folding on backbones stripped to bare coordinates, twilight-zone remote homology below 15% sequence identity, function prediction against experimentally evidenced annotation, alanine-scan ranking in monomers and across interfaces, de novo fold and motif design, and sixteen-round closed-loop binder design against an AlphaFold2 oracle.

Two devices do the separating. Targets are stratified by how far each one sits from anything that existed before the training cutoff, measured structurally rather than assumed from a deposition date. And every ranking panel pairs each true hotspot with a neutral decoy of the same amino acid, which holds any method reading only the residue letter to a 50% win rate. Models run in a no-code track — weights and chain-of-thought only — and a with-code track with air-gapped NumPy and SciPy, which separates arithmetic limits from missing biophysics.

Task Explorer

How the data is preparedTarget selection, how novelty is measured, and the holdout split behind every figure

Every prompt strips PDB IDs, gene symbols, organism names, and alignments. All 522 targets (702 calls per track) are filterable by stratum in the datapoint browser.

Task 1 · Forward folding — 100 targets

Each candidate was structurally searched against the pre-May-2026 PDB; its highest TM-score to any prior chain sets its structural novelty (TM > 0.5 shares a fold; < 0.3 is random). Designed proteins are grouped separately by provenance.

StratumnDepositedBest pre-cutoff matchDefinition
Known (pre-2026)151987 – 2020TM 0.87 – 1.00Pre-cutoff PDB positive control.
Homolog gradient122026TM 0.65 – 0.94New entries with a close pre-cutoff structural homolog.
PDB-novel272026TM 0.53 – 0.81Natural 2026 proteins with only partial structural precedent.
De novo282026TM 0.45 – 0.91Computationally designed folds with no evolutionary homologs.
Truly novel182026TM 0.33 – 0.53No pre-cutoff PDB chain reaches the 0.50 same-fold line.

Task 2 · Inverse folding — 100 targets

Same 100 proteins and five strata as Task 1. Inputs keep only Cα coordinates (every residue relabelled UNK), backbone dihedrals, and Cα burial counts. Wild-type sequences were refolded through the same ESMFold-2 pipeline to set the 0.885 ceiling.

Task 3 · Remote homology — 120 pairs

SCOPe domain pairs split by which search method fails (30 pairs per rung; rungs 2–4 matched near 11% identity). Released files carry SCOPe families, sequence identity, and Smith–Waterman scores; the Foldseek E-values separating rungs 2 and 3 are not stored in the file.

RungnSequence identitySelection rule
1 · Sequence-easy3018 – 38% (med. 23%)Same SCOPe superfamily; recovered by Smith–Waterman.
2 · Structure-caught309 – 14% (med. 11%)Same superfamily; sequence alignment fails, Foldseek 3Di hits.
3 · Deep twilight308 – 16% (med. 11%)Same superfamily; both sequence and Foldseek search fail.
4 · Matched decoy309 – 14% (med. 11%)Different superfamilies matched on structural class and identity.

Task 4 · Function prediction — 60 proteins

QuickGO targets graded strictly on experimentally evidenced Gene Ontology terms. Date caveat: post_may_2026 (n=11) has 7 entries dated 2026-07-25 and 4 pre-cutoff entries (2025-11-19 / 2026-03-31); early_2026_uniprot (n=49) spans 2022-02-03 to 2026-01-08 with 47 sharing the bulk date 2025-10-27. The true post-cutoff holdout is 7 proteins.

Task 5 · Monomer alanine ranking — 52 panels

Each 18-candidate panel pairs 6 hotspots, 6 moderate sites, and 6 same-AA decoys (holding residue-letter lookup to 50%), drawn across four experimental readouts.

SourcenMeasured quantity
De novo miniproteins24Folding ΔΔG (MegaScale); designed folds with no natural homologs.
Natural proteins14Folding ΔΔG on natural folds.
MaveDB deep scans12Post-cutoff deep mutational scanning activity.
Stability and function2Paired stability and activity on the same protein.

Task 6 · Interface binding ranking — 38 complexes

Interface X→Ala panels graded on measured binding ΔΔG after removing monomer-destabilising mutations. Split by pre-2026 PDB presence: 31 in known_pdb_pre2026 and 7 in unseen_or_post2026.

Task 7 · De novo and motif design — 40 specifications

Forty written specs graded on five single-shot gates: sequence hygiene, <30% identity to natural parents, ESMFold-2/OpenFold3 agreement (scRMSD ≤ 2 Å), pLDDT ≥ 80, and the structural gate below.

KindnLengthStructural gate
Fold-conditioned2464 – 136 AARefolded design reaches TM ≥ 0.50 against the target fold.
Motif scaffolding1670 – 128 AAHeld crystal motif stays within Cα RMSD ≤ 1.5 Å.

Task 8 · Closed-loop binder design — 12 epitopes

Twelve target chains with five hotspot residues each; methods get 16 binder proposals (55–85 AA) scored by AlphaFold2 and ESMFold-2. Only the third group is a post-cutoff crystal holdout.

Running the benchmark

# unit, anti-cheat and leakage tests
.venv/bin/pytest -v

# CPU-graded tasks 1, 3, 4, 5, 6
.venv/bin/python scripts/run_benchmark_llms.py --provider openai --model gpt-6.2-sol --stages 1,3,4,5,6 --thinking-budget 4000

# closed-loop AlphaFold2 binder campaigns
.venv/bin/python scripts/run_stage3b_closed_loop_llms.py --provider anthropic --model claude-fable-5-2 --mode closed_loop --oracle modal_af2
